messages:
david.eng: Quick question for people-ops — we promoted an individual who transferred from EMEA contract->FTE on 2025-01-10. Manager wants salary effective 2025-01-01 and to treat the equity grant as if they were converted on Jan 1 (so cliff starts then). Is any of that doable?

emily.hr: Two parts: base pay retro and equity/grant effective date. For retro base pay we can sometimes do a payroll adjustment; equity/grant dates are stricter.

lucy.payroll: Payroll rules (EMEA): local payroll runs, tax/social withholding differences, and currency conversion matter. We can post a retro adjustment for base pay up to 60 days without an off-cycle run; beyond that it's an off-cycle and requires finance sign-off. Jan 1 -> today is >60 days so expect off-cycle. Also need GL codes and the local payroll approver.

thomas.comp: From comp perspective: we can approve retroactive base salary if there's strong business rationale, but we cannot backdate the grant issuance date to before the legal hire/convert date. Equity requires the person to be on the books as an FTE at grant time; system/legal prevents pre-dating RSU grants.

david.eng: Ok that's a bummer on equity. Any workaround? Manager really wants cliff to start earlier so new hire accruals align with team expectations.

emily.hr: Workarounds: 1) offer a one-time retention/spot cash payment to mirror the value of "missed" vesting time, or 2) issue an additional pro-rated grant with a custom vesting schedule (legal + comp must approve). Both require approvals and tax implications.

thomas.comp: If you go route (2), comp needs: a) the proposed grant amount, b) target vesting schedule, c) why standard grant wouldn't suffice. We'll fast-track if the impact is clear.

lucy.payroll: For cash/one-time payments in EMEA we also need to calculate employer social contributions - sometimes those make cash heavier than equity. Please put local payroll contact in the packet.

recruiter.ops: For hiring ops, if this internal movement frees a headcount, start the backfill req but mark it as "internal movement pending" in the description and link the promo ticket. Recruiters can begin sourcing but label offers conditional on promo finalization. Req ID helps with GL coding later.

emily.hr: Minimal exception packet we need: 1) Manager justification (3 bullets: scope, impact, reason for retro) 2) Dates: original contract end, conversion date, requested effective date 3) Proposed compensation adjustments (base delta, cash amount or additional grant) 4) Approvers list (mgr, comp, finance, legal) 5) Local payroll contact + req ID if backfill. Paste into the exception form.

david.eng: Can you paste a tiny copyable template I can drop into the form?

emily.hr: Sure, small template to paste:

``
Exception packet (one-paragraph + bullets):
- Employee: Jane Doe, region: UK, current status: contractor -> FTE (conversion date: 2025-01-10)
- Requested effective date: 2025-01-01
- Ask: retro base pay to requested date, and equity cliff to align with requested date (see rationale)
- Rationale: took over X product area on 2024-11-20, drove Y (metrics + outcome), manager expected promo during conversion
- Proposed remediation: cash payment of £X to compensate for 1 month of missed base + additional pro-rated grant of Z RSUs, vesting schedule proposed: 25% at 12 months, then quarterly thereafter
- Approvers: Manager (david.eng), Director (sarah.dir), Comp (thomas.comp), Finance (lucy.payroll), Legal (legal-team)
- Local payroll contact: pauline.uk.payroll, Req ID (if backfill): REQ-2025-0456
``

thomas.comp: Add a line with the suggested target salary band and local currency range — that speeds approval.

hr-bot: Reminder: attach any documented manager communications (emails/slack) showing the expectation set at conversion. Tag @thomas.comp and @lucy.payroll in the approvers list.

emily.hr: Note on employee-facing language: we won't say "exception" in the offer/notice. We'll communicate the final decision and effective date.

david.eng: Thanks all. I'll assemble the packet and drop in the exception form now. I'll DM the comp docs to @thomas.comp for pre-review.

emily.hr: Great — ping when submitted and we'll triage intake within 72 hours. :thumbsup:
